title: Group with parentheses
objective: Use parentheses to choose the order of a calculation or a condition, and read a mixed condition correctly.

body.text: Parentheses ( and ) group part of an expression, and the part inside them is worked out first. You can use them in a calculation, in a condition, or in both. Without them, Lagom follows its usual order: multiply and divide before add and subtract, and and before or.

body.title: Parentheses in a calculation
body.code:
make base equal to 2
make bonus equal to 3
make multiplier equal to 4
make total equal to (base plus bonus) times multiplier
say total
make cost equal to 10
make count equal to 4
make average equal to cost divided by (count plus 1)
say average

body.text: Parentheses matter in conditions too. The first condition below asks whether the person is old enough and allowed, or is an administrator. Without the brackets, the and would bind differently and change the meaning.

body.title: Parentheses in a condition
body.code:
make age equal to 15
make allowed equal to true
make administrator equal to false
if (age is greater than 13 and allowed) or administrator
    say "allowed"
make blocked equal to false
make banned equal to false
make safe equal to not (blocked or banned)
say safe

body.prompt: The program prints 14 because multiplication happens first. It should print 20 instead.
body.starter:
make total equal to 2 plus 3 times 4
say total
body.solution:
make total equal to (2 plus 3) times 4
say total
